problem:
Consider the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{x},\,y(1)=2.
$$

Use the tangent line approximation of $y(x)$ at $x=1$ to approximate $y(1.5).$
worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $y(x)$ at the point $a=1$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(a)+{y}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =y(1)+{y}^{′}(1)(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

From the initial condition, we know that $y(1)=2.$ We also know that ${y}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{x},$ so

$$
{y}^{′}(1)=\frac{1}{1}=1.
$$

Substituting our values for $y(1)$ and ${y}^{′}(1)$ into our expression for $L(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(1)+{y}^{′}(1)(x-1) \\  & =2+(1)(x-1) \\  & =x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can approximate $y(1.5)$ using $L(1.5).$ We get

$$
y(1.5)≈L(1.5)=1.5+1=2.5.
$$
